edges.description: Activating GNAS mutation raises intracellular cAMP and drives mucin gene expression via the Gs-cAMP-PKA pathway.
KRAS-MAPK/PI3K signaling drives neoplastic proliferation of appendiceal epithelium.
Accumulating mucin distends the appendiceal lumen, thinning and weakening the wall.

The proliferating mucinous neoplasm expands within and distends the appendix. No direct quantitative evidence isolates proliferation (as distinct from mucin secretion) as the driver of luminal distension; retained as a mechanistic description without an evidence claim per the evidence SOP.

A subset of neoplasms progresses to high-grade and invasive disease, associated with acquisition of TP53 mutations, consistent with a stepwise LAMN -> HAMN -> mucinous adenocarcinoma morphologic transition.
Released neoplastic mucin disseminates and accumulates on peritoneal surfaces.
High-grade tumors invade the appendiceal wall and disseminate to lymph nodes and distant organs.

nodes.description: Simple appendectomy is the primary and appropriate definitive treatment for small (< 1 cm) localized low-risk lesions, including small tip-located neuroendocrine tumors and LAMN confined to the appendix with clear margins; larger lesions (> 2 cm) require right hemicolectomy.

nodes.description: Progressive intraluminal mucin accumulation distends the appendix (mucocele), thins the muscular wall, and can culminate in rupture of the visceral peritoneum, releasing neoplastic mucin into the peritoneal cavity.

nodes.description: For pseudomyxoma peritonei and disseminated mucinous disease, cytoreductive surgery (peritonectomy, omentectomy, and resection of involved organs) combined with hyperthermic intraperitoneal chemotherapy is the standard of care in specialized centers, targeting residual microscopic peritoneal disease.

nodes.description: Constitutive Gs-cAMP-PKA signaling from mutant GNAS markedly upregulates the gel-forming mucins MUC2 and MUC5AC, producing the copious mucin that is the hallmark of low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms.

Signet ring cell carcinoma is the most aggressive high-grade variant.

nodes.description: Appendiceal mucinous neoplasms are driven by activating somatic mutations in the KRAS oncogene (codons 12/13) and the GNAS oncogene (codon 201). KRAS activation engages downstream MAPK and PI3K signaling to drive proliferation and survival, while activating GNAS mutations constitutively activate the stimulatory G protein alpha subunit. In appendiceal mucinous tumors KRAS and GNAS mutations frequently co-occur, and GNAS is characteristically enriched in low-grade lesions.

evidence.snippet: A mutational analysis identified activating GNAS mutations in 16 of 32 low-grade appendiceal mucinous neoplasms (LAMNs) but in none of three mucinous adenocarcinomas (MACs). KRAS mutations were found in 30 LAMNs and in all MACs.

nodes.description: KRAS-driven mitogenic signaling produces neoplastic proliferation of appendiceal epithelium, generating the mucinous or glandular tumor mass. In the low-grade mucinous setting the proliferative advantage is modest and combined with the secretory (mucinous) phenotype rather than aggressive growth.

nodes.description: Intraperitoneal accumulation of mucinous ascites and mucin-producing neoplastic implants coating peritoneal surfaces and abdominal viscera, following spread from a ruptured appendiceal mucinous neoplasm. Characterized by the redistribution phenomenon, progressive abdominal distension, and functional gastrointestinal obstruction.

evidence.snippet: Over time, mucin accumulation in the peritoneal cavity gradually causes massive symptomatic distension and functional gastrointestinal obstruction.

nodes.description: Right hemicolectomy with regional lymphadenectomy is used for invasive adenocarcinoma, HAMN, and higher-risk or larger neuroendocrine tumors, removing the tumor and regional nodes analogously to colorectal cancer surgery.

evidence.snippet: Early-stage cancers can be treated definitively with surgery, and selected patients derive long-term benefit from cytoreductive surgery and heated intraperitoneal chemotherapy (HIPEC).

nodes.description: Systemic chemotherapy, largely extrapolated from colorectal cancer regimens (fluoropyrimidines with oxaliplatin or irinotecan), is used for unresectable or metastatic appendiceal adenocarcinoma and high-grade disease, though the evidence base is limited by the rarity of these tumors.

evidence.snippet: Appendiceal neoplasms are heterogeneous and are often treated with chemotherapy similarly to colorectal cancer (CRC).

nodes.description: Acquisition of TP53 mutation (mutually exclusive with GNAS) marks progression to high-grade and invasive appendiceal cancer. Loss of p53 function impairs DNA-damage response and apoptosis, enabling infiltrative invasion and metastatic potential; TP53 mutation status independently predicts survival.

evidence.snippet: GNAS and TP53 were mutually exclusive (Bonferroni corrected P < .001). Tumor grade and TP53 mutation status independently predicted OS.
